text: A single ACL record isn't limited to just a role check. It can combine a role requirement, a condition, and a script, all on the very same ACL. These aren't alternative ways of writing the same rule, offering a choice between them. When more than one is present, they stack together, and understanding exactly how they stack is the difference between an admin who reads an ACL correctly and one who's only guessing.

The roles an ACL requires live in a related list called Requires role at the bottom of the form, not a single dropdown value, and a user needs at least one of the listed roles for this part of the check to pass. List three roles on an ACL, and any user holding even one of those three satisfies the requirement, an OR within the role list itself. Leave that related list empty, and the role check is simply skipped, not automatically failed.

The Condition field is a lightweight, no-code builder for straightforward field comparisons, something like active is true or priority is critical. When logic needs more than a direct comparison, like checking whether the current user belongs to a referenced group, the Script field takes over instead, using a current variable just like a business rule, and explicitly setting answer true or answer false. There's no implicit pass if the script never sets that variable.

A realistic example for incident.assignment_group would be a script checking whether the current user is a member of the group referenced in current.assignment_group, setting answer true only if they are. That's exactly the kind of lookup the simple condition builder genuinely cannot express on its own.

Here's the part worth memorizing precisely: if an ACL has roles listed and also a condition or script, both have to pass. It is never either the role matches, or the condition passes. A user holding the required role who fails the script is still denied by that very same ACL. Role and condition or script combine with AND, exactly the same AND relationship that governs how whole ACLs combine with each other. It's AND all the way down, at every single layer.
